content: Atmit is a nutritional supplement specifically designed to combat famine in impoverished regions. This creamy and nutrient-rich food originates from Ethiopia and is now widely utilized to nourish severely malnourished and weakened individuals, including both adults and children. The term atmit is derived from the Ethiopian language and translates to thin, nourishing porridge. The preparation of atmit involves a combination of rolled oats, powdered milk, powdered sugar, vitamins, and minerals. It is formulated to be easily digestible and is rich in both protein and calories, making it an ideal dietary solution for individuals who are unable to consume solid foods due to severe malnutrition. A Christian relief organization adapted the recipe for production in the United States to facilitate its shipment to Ethiopia and other African nations. During the famine of 1985 and 1986, Project Mercy delivered 930 tons of atmit to Ethiopia. World Vision relief workers utilized this supply to prepare millions of hot, nutritious meals, which played a critical role in strengthening individuals debilitated by famine. Various charitable and relief organizations have developed different formulations of this porridge to meet specific needs. For instance, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints created a formula for atmit that was sent to Niger in 2005. This particular formulation consisted of 50% fine oatmeal flour, 25% nonfat milk, 20% sugar, and 5% vitamins and minerals. In recent years, atmit has been distributed to numerous countries, including Uganda, Sudan, South Africa, Haiti, Gaza, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and Niger, as part of ongoing efforts to address malnutrition and famine in vulnerable populations.
